# Berlin Rent Increase Review Checklist

A rent increase after minor repairs is not automatically valid. Before replying, verify the timing, the legal basis the landlord is relying on, and whether the request is really a rent increase or a separate cost item.

# What to Check Before You Respond

## Key facts to review
- **Lease start:** 2024-03-01
- **Notice date:** 2026-02-10
- **Proposed effective date:** 2026-05-01
- **Type of increase claimed:** regular increase, modernization-related increase, index rent, staff/operating costs, or something else
- **Reason given:** minor repairs, maintenance, improvement, or modernization
- **Current rent structure:** cold rent, warm rent, and any separate service charges

## Documents and points to gather
- Your signed lease and all addenda
- The landlord’s written notice, including the exact reason and calculation
- Any repair notices, contractor letters, or work descriptions
- Before/after photos if the work was in your unit
- Previous rent increase letters, if any
- Rent payment history
- Operating cost statements, if the landlord is mixing in additional charges
- Any correspondence where the landlord described the work as repair rather than improvement
- Evidence of when you received the notice, if relevant

## Timing and content checks
- Whether the notice is in writing and clearly states the amount, reason, and start date
- Whether the stated effective date leaves enough lead time under the lease and applicable rules
- Whether the landlord is trying to charge for work that sounds like ordinary maintenance
- Whether the increase is being tied to a specific legal basis and calculation
- Whether the total rent would exceed any limits or caps that may apply
- Whether the increase is separate from service-charge adjustments

## Practical red flags
- The notice says “repair” but charges you as if it were a value-adding upgrade
- The landlord gives no calculation or only a vague explanation
- The increase starts very soon after the notice without a clear legal basis
- The landlord combines repairs, modernization, and operating costs in one unclear letter
- The notice lacks a clear breakdown of what part of the rent is changing

# Polite Email Draft to Request Clarification

Subject: Request for clarification regarding proposed rent increase

Dear [Landlord’s Name],

Thank you for your notice dated 2026-02-10 regarding the proposed rent increase.

Before I respond, I would appreciate a written clarification of the legal and factual basis for the increase, including:
- the exact reason for the increase,
- whether the work was intended as repair, maintenance, or modernization,
- the calculation used to determine the new amount,
- which part of the rent would change,
- and any documents supporting the request.

For reference, my tenancy began on 2024-03-01, and the proposed effective date is 2026-05-01.

Please also confirm whether the increase is separate from any operating-cost or service-charge adjustment.

Thank you for your help. I look forward to your clarification.

Kind regards,
[Your Name]
[Your Address]

# Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Review lease] https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/
Action: [Button: Tenant advice] https://www.berliner-mieterverein.de/
Action: [Button: Consumer help] https://www.verbraucherzentrale.de/

# Sources

- German Civil Code (BGB): https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/
- Berlin Tenants’ Association: https://www.berliner-mieterverein.de/
- Consumer advice center: https://www.verbraucherzentrale.de/

- Do not invent local placeholder paths such as /image.jpg or /asset/foo.png.
